# Independent audit of canonical source-plane reduction

Audited `candidate c106b596b70bfd05`, including its added Section 4a, against the actual source-transport, sampled-majorant, and nonregular common-separator dependencies. The mathematical reductions PASS within their stated positive-fiber, attained-minimum hypotheses. The physical-certificate extension in Section 4a is justified by the explicit argument below. No cap-payment conclusion follows from the reduction alone.

## 1. Interpolation and the face cover

The interpolation statement (1) uses actual proper deepest marks, not arbitrary points in the convex hull of the sources. The convex buffered superlevel and strict base-depth superlevel place an integer average in the proper deepest set. An attained own-proper cap there gives exact equality of its quantile thresholds. Concavity of the buffer forces equality of buffer values; positivity and strict monotonicity of the weighted geometric mean then force equality of L-values. Unique fiber-interior deepest marks identify the averaged mark. The argument works for a finite positive combination, including an integer average whose source coefficient is zero.

Every lattice point of the finite source hull lies in the relative interior of its minimal face, which extends to a maximal occupied face. The faces therefore cover the source set. If two selected relative-interior integer witnesses have the same parity, their midpoint is an integer whose minimal face is the join of the two faces. Distinct maximal occupied faces would then be strictly contained in another occupied face. This proves the distinct-parity count without a disjointness assertion about the faces. It uses at most the occupied parities of the actual complete base, hence at most 2^n.

A relative-interior witness admits a representation by every source of its face with strictly positive coefficients. The finite sampled touching-majorant lemma applies there because the deepest mark is interior in its positive continuous fiber, even if its base is on the boundary of the projection. The Farkas construction supplies a finite base slope. Equality of the averaged nonnegative sampled gaps proves that the same plane touches every original positive source of the face.

## 2. Sampled identity and row preservation

Let V be the minimum of the selected sampled majorants. Affinity makes each majorant positive on the canonical hull, and finiteness makes V strictly positive there. On every sampled fiber V>=L; at every original positive source V=L. Testing the original cone certificate with the concave function V gives

    1 = integral V dmu >= integral V dnu >= integral L dnu = 1.

The target has a strictly positive density relative to d-volume on each positive sampled fiber. The continuous nonnegative sampled gap must therefore vanish everywhere on that fiber, including its boundary. This proves V=L on the sampled union.

The argument makes no claim that V=L at unsampled real bases. Before replacement a sampled plane may fall below the old extension there. Accordingly, the old convex row container is C intersect {A<=L}, not an asserted globally nonnegative zero set. After replacement every chosen A majorizes V globally and its contact set is convex.

Every retained original row has the same barycenter, sampled L-values, and source value. Hence its V expectation is its source V-value. If a new affine majorant A touches its source, its affine expectation is the same number, so the row is supported on A=V. No row is replaced or relabeled by a uniform cell law.

## 3. The SAME physical separator survives

This assertion requires that the original coefficients and rows came from the actual joint physical/parameter separator. An arbitrary parameter certificate cannot be promoted to a physical separator by this argument.

Fix that original joint separator, including all cap weights, proper contact weights, supporting-face selections, section allocations, and scale coefficient. In the audited nonregular response formula, the pure-body coefficients depend on the sampled values of L and log L, the original source marks and their buffer values, the bodies, energies, covariance, and the fixed cap data. These are all unchanged. The continuous source gradients are also unchanged, because V=L on the whole positive source fiber and the source is interior. Thus the pure-body stress, normal-variable identities, scale identity, and original physical inequality remain exactly the same.

It is unnecessary, and generally unjustified, to claim that the new radial cone is contained in the old radial cone. Instead let h+cV be concave on the relevant common neighborhood, with c>=0. Apply Jensen in EACH RETAINED row and use the exact rowwise V moment:

    E_row h + c E_row V <= h(source)+c V(source),
    E_row h <= h(source).

Summing with the unchanged source weights proves the required parameter inequality for h. The same proof works for the cone restricted to C. For simultaneous body motions, the finite positive-plane representative has a positive neighborhood extension, so the actual path V+t h is feasible for small t after exact logarithmic normalization, just as in the applicability theorem.

The actual separated response is the sum of its pure-body, raw-parameter, cap-normal, and scale parts. The unchanged pure-body inequality, the just-proved new parameter inequality, and unchanged signed-coordinate equalities therefore verify EVERY new joint test with the SAME original separator. No second compactness selection is needed. In particular the original theta law is retained; it is not replaced by a new parameter-only cap law.

One must still keep the original physical sources and weights when using subsequent stress or cap formulas. The new geometric plane anchors may have zero original source weight and are not substitutes for those sources.

## 4. Optional certificate contraction

The feasible source coefficient set is compact: it is an intersection of closed halfspaces in a finite simplex, with total mass fixed by the two constant tests. Choosing a quadratic-minimizing certificate is therefore legitimate. For an integer positive-weight average of distinct positive source bases, interpolation gives both its actual allowed mark and exact L-affinity. Jensen for h+cL preserves every cone inequality under the mass contraction. Strict convexity of the full squared norm strictly lowers the objective because the distinct base coordinates make the source points distinct. This proves both parity separation and the empty-lattice-polytope conclusion.

That operation may change the source coefficients, rows, body-response coefficients, and their relation to cap laws. It proves a parameter-only reduction. Nothing above licenses using it in place of the SAME physical source law. The note states this distinction correctly.

## 5. Constants, degeneracy, and consequences for rates

The reduction costs no extra parity factor: at most k(P)<=2^n planes suffice. Rank-zero base hulls give one covering face and one plane. Zero original source coefficients are harmless at the new anchors, because deepestness and source-interiority estimates concern all proper deepest marks. Repeated continuous gradients and sampled whole-fiber ties are retained; almost-everywhere continuous gradients are unchanged on each positive fiber.

The result is proved in the positive d-dimensional fiber setting inherited from its dependencies; it is not itself a treatment of the original conjecture's intrinsic lower-dimensional cases or d=0. That restriction is explicit in the standing use of interior marks and positive continuous fibers and should not be broadened without the separate reductions.

Each new global geometric cell contains its anchored proper deepest mark at positive L-height. Thus its global maximum height has a uniform positive lower bound whenever the inherited source-value bounds are uniform. This excludes a delayed start for the ENTIRE global cell. It does not exclude delayed starts of the cell restricted to another fixed sampled fiber. Nor does it place a slice center at the anchor base, preserve a naive closed cap indicator under anisotropic blow-up, or split the global stress by cells. These remain separate obligations.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
